newsitem.title: GERMANY: W.German business sentiment rose in September - Ifo.
newsitem.headline: W.German business sentiment rose in September - Ifo.

text.p: Germany's Ifo economic research institute said on Friday its business climate index for west Germany, a key measure of business confidence, rose to 95.7 in September from 94.4 in August, the highest level in 12 months.
The rise was slightly above market forecasts which had ranged from 95 to 95.5. Economists said the figure showed the economic recovery was continuing at a moderate pace and was far from overheating.
The Bundesbank therefore had no need to either cut or raise interest rates in the foreseeable future, they said.
"It reflects the trend shown in order and production data which showed a fairly strong rise in July and August," said Uwe Angenendt, an economist at BHF Bank in Frankfurt.
He predicted German gross domestic product (GDP) would show a rise of about percent in the third quarter from the second quarter, compared with 1.5 percent growth in the second quarter.
The Ifo data was keenly awaited but had little impact on financial markets, with share and bond dealers shrugging off the rise because it was only slightly above forecasts.
In August, the west German index had shown more modest growth to 90.4 from 90.0.
Ifo's east German business climate rose only marginally in September, to 104.0 from 103.9.

Economists said the east German data was not very informative because it was subject to sharp monthly swings. In addition, the region's industry had shrunk so much in recent years that its importance for pan-German growth was limited.
